Keywords: Laude Hymn Marches and Anti Corruption
RagShortTexts: Apocalyptic fear in 1260 sparked mass Flagellant marches across Italy, scourging flesh to.

Variants.Content: Many people in northern Italy believed that the apocalyptic third age prophesied by Joachim of Fiore would arrive in 1260, and that belief set off mass hysteria. The Flagellant movement began in Perugia, where the hermit Raniero Fasani led bands of penitents through the streets, and it spread quickly to other cities. Penitents stripped to the waist, marched under black banners, and flogged their backs with leather scourges tipped with iron, believing that their own blood could atone for the sins of the world. Cities and their clergy watched with alarm as the crowds grew into tens of thousands, and some towns opened their gates to them while others dreaded the disorder that followed.

The first enthusiasm of the processions eased old feuds, and rival families sometimes laid down their arms to march together. As the wandering bands began to denounce ecclesiastical corruption and claim the right to grant absolution, the authorities moved to outlaw their assemblies.
Dusty miles of barefoot penitents chant mournful laude hymns. The sickening thud of leather knotted with steel tearing into bare backs terrifies onlookers into falling on their knees.
